admission.justification: Both the settings pin and install-day resolution were seriously available and rejected for stated reasons, and every later host release now has to move the contract, the lock and the consumers together.

alternatives.option: Name the host package and one exact release in a packaged contract, ship the whole npm lock, and make every reader take the version from the contract.
alternatives.reason: The release then moves only with a release of the product, two installs of one build hold the same host package for package, and a foreign settings value can no longer select an untested host.

alternatives.option: Keep paseoRuntime.version as the pin and refuse a block that names another version.
alternatives.reason: A user's settings file would still be able to hold a build at a host version the build was not made for, and a release could not move the host at all.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The host becomes a real dependency of the Python package or publishes a supported stable plugin interface, so one build can track several host releases.

alternatives.option: Resolve the host packages on the day of the install from a manifest range, as npm does by default.
alternatives.reason: The host's own packages state ranges; resolving them at install time makes the installed host a different tree on every machine and leaves no release-owned lock to check.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The host vendor publishes lock guarantees or a supported compatibility range the build can trust.

consequences: A host release change is a product release step: the contract, the host manifest and the lock move together and the release concordance check refuses a mismatch.
A settings block whose version names another release loads and produces one notice; it never changes which release is installed or compared.
context: Before this leaf the host version was a required key of the user's paseoRuntime settings block, so a build could not move the host and a settings file could name any version of a package whose plugin support is explicitly unpromised. The build shipped no host lock, so 8 dependencies of the host's command line and 29 of its server were resolved on the day of the install.
decider: developer direction D75 (2026-10-06), refined by the architect and frozen in MIK-R96@v1 rule 2
